subject: Social Habits
title: My family
subtopics: What my family does for me
objectives: Children will name people in their family.
Children will say one way they show love to their family.
content: Who is in my family, what my family does for me, and showing love to my family.
teachingActivities: Welcome every kind of family: children may live with parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles, guardians or siblings; never ask a child to explain a family situation; use family photographs only if the family agrees; use home-language words for family members and repeat them in English.
learnerActivities: Name people in their family and show or say love to a family member.
resources: A doll family or picture cards
assessment: Observe whether each child names at least two family members and shows love in a simple way.
expectedOutcomes: Names at least two family members.
Shows or says love to a family member.

lessons.title: Who is in my family?
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will name people who are in their family.
successCriteria: Names one or two family members
Points to a family picture card
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness and safety in Term 1.
resources: Picture cards: mother, father, baby, grandma, grandpa, brother, sister
lessons.starter: Hold up the doll family and say "This is a family. Every family is special."
teacherActivities: Show each picture card and say the family word.
Say "Who is in your family?" and wait.
Let children share a home-language word for a family member.
Sing the family song with actions.
learnerActivities: Children look and repeat the word.
Child names or points to a person.
Child says the word if they wish.
Children sing and do actions.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture card and say the family word. Children: Children look and repeat the word.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Who is in your family?" and wait. Children: Child names or points to a person.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children share a home-language word for a family member. Children: Child says the word if they wish.
Step 4. Teacher: Sing the family song with actions. Children: Children sing and do actions.

practical.title: Family cards
steps: Choose a card for your family.
practical.safety: Never ask a child to explain their family situation and accept every kind of family. Use photographs only with parents’ agreement.

differentiation.support: Name the family members together with the cards.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say a family member’s name and what they do.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Who is in your family?
questions.expected: Mother, father, sister or other person.

expectedOutcomes: Names at least one family member
Points to a family picture card
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "I love my family."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about family members with your child and name each one.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name people who are in their family" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: My family, my family, I love my family.

lessons.title: What my family does for me
lessons.subject: Social Habits
lessons.subtopic: What my family does for me
objectives: Children will say one thing their family does for them.
successCriteria: Says or shows one thing a family member does
Says thank you to the family with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness and safety in Term 1.
resources: Pictures: cooking, bathing, reading, playing, hugging
lessons.starter: Show a picture of someone cooking and say "Someone cooks for me. My family helps me."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say what the family member does.
Ask "Who cooks for you?" and listen.
Act out looking after a baby doll with kindness.
Say "We say thank you to our family."
learnerActivities: Children look and say the action.
Child points to a person or says a word.
Child rocks or feeds the doll gently.
Children say thank you together.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say what the family member does. Children: Children look and say the action.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Who cooks for you?" and listen. Children: Child points to a person or says a word.
Step 3. Teacher: Act out looking after a baby doll with kindness. Children: Child rocks or feeds the doll gently.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We say thank you to our family." Children: Children say thank you together.

practical.title: Family helpers
practical.safety: Keep pictures gentle and accept every child’s answer. Be sensitive to children whose home circumstances are difficult.

differentiation.support: Show a picture and say the action together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say two things their family does.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say to them?

expectedOutcomes: Says one thing a family member does
Says thank you to the family
lessons.conclusion: Hug the doll and say "I am thankful."
lessons.homeConnection: Thank each family member for something small each day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say one thing their family does for them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Showing love
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will show love to family members in simple ways.
successCriteria: Makes a heart or gives a smile
Says "I love you" or waves with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness and safety in Term 1.
resources: A paper heart for each child
lessons.starter: Show a paper heart and say "A heart means love. We can show love to our family."
teacherActivities: Show how to colour a heart for a family member.
Help each child write or mark their name on the heart.
Practise saying "I love you" or giving a smile and wave.
learnerActivities: Children colour a heart.
Child makes a mark on the heart.
Child names or points to a person.
Child says or shows love.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to colour a heart for a family member. Children: Children colour a heart.
Step 2. Teacher: Help each child write or mark their name on the heart. Children: Child makes a mark on the heart.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Who is the heart for?" Children: Child names or points to a person.
Step 4. Teacher: Practise saying "I love you" or giving a smile and wave. Children: Child says or shows love.

practical.title: Heart for my family
practical.safety: Use non-toxic crayons and supervise closely. Never force a child to say I love you; accept a smile or a wave.

differentiation.support: Colour together and say the family name.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to colour two hearts.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Makes a heart for a family member
Shows love in a simple way
lessons.conclusion: Sing the family song and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Give the heart to a family member and say thank you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show love to family members in simple ways" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Family helping game
lessons.subject: Social Habits
lessons.subtopic: What my family does for me
objectives: Children will act out how family members help each other.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness and safety in Term 1.
lessons.starter: Set up a play house and say "Let us play family and help each other."
teacherActivities: Show how to feed a doll and put it to bed.
Let children choose a role such as mother, father or child.
Say "How can we help?" and let children act.
Say thank you for the help.
learnerActivities: Children watch.
Child chooses a role.
Child acts out a helping job.
Children say thank you to friends.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to feed a doll and put it to bed. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children choose a role such as mother, father or child. Children: Child chooses a role.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "How can we help?" and let children act. Children: Child acts out a helping job.
Step 4. Teacher: Say thank you for the help. Children: Children say thank you to friends.

practical.title: Play family
practical.safety: Keep toys large and clean and supervise sharing. Respect every child’s idea of family.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child and suggest a job.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the helper who thanks the others.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says help or thank you in play
lessons.conclusion: Tidy the play house and say "We help."
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child help with a small job and say thank you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "act out how family members help each other" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 family check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child talks about family and shows love.
successCriteria: Shows love in a simple way
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness and safety in Term 1.
lessons.starter: Sing the family song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: family cards, hearts and play house.
At each station ask "Who is in your family?" and watch.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or action.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: family cards, hearts and play house. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "Who is in your family?" and watch. Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Family stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and be sensitive to every family situation. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell a friend about their family.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names family members; says what the family does; shows love; helps in play.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep talking about family and showing love at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child talks about family and shows love" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
